Retinal cone dysfunction causes impaired color vision and reduced visual acuity; no independent neurologic disease is established.
Multivitamin transport deficiency with infantile neurodegeneration; IgG deficiency in 2/2 supports immune dysfunction. Nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage.
Primary bladder adenocarcinoma with enteric differentiation; colonic histology does not establish gastrointestinal origin or involvement.
Noninfectious inflammation of the meninges; this umbrella includes causes that are neither autoimmune nor immune-mediated.
Congenital common arterial trunk with aortic dominance is a structural cardiovascular malformation.
Solid malignant pleuropulmonary tumor; aggressive behavior alone does not establish common damage to other organs.
Congenital neural tube closure defects include anencephaly and spina bifida, affecting neural structures and associated skull or vertebral development.
Inherited renal tubulointerstitial disease; retinal degeneration in 1/3 meets the approximate 30% threshold. Anemia is secondary to kidney failure.
Inherited organic acid metabolism disorders; direct toxic or metabolic brain injury is common, approximately ≥30% across typical clinical cases; milder subtypes vary.
Congenital inward rotation of the eyelid; associated corneal irritation and scarring remain within the ocular axis.
Renal tubular maldevelopment causes persistent oligohydramnios; pulmonary hypoplasia and joint/limb deformities are defining Potter-sequence manifestations.
